title: Apple and Epic argue over how much Apple should get from purchases made outside the App Store
summary: Apple has proposed a fee structure for digital purchases made through external links outside the App Store, though it cannot currently collect commissions after a 2025 court ruling. Epic Games opposes Apple's proposal as exceeding the court's guidance on App Store monopoly practices. The dispute continues the ongoing legal battle between the companies over commission structures.
content:
In a new filing in its long-running legal dispute with Epic Games, Apple has proposed a structure that would allow it to collect fees on digital purchases made via external links that don't use the company's in-app purchase system. Epic has already responded, saying that Apple's request is "far outside of the bounds" of the court's guidance.
Right now, Apple cannot take a commission on external purchases after California district court judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers ruled in April 2025 that found the company "willfully" didn't comply with her 2021 Epic Games v. Apple injunction. However, a Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals panel said that Apple  …
Read the full story at The Verge.

zh.summary: 苹果提出了一项关于通过应用商店外部链接进行的数字购买的费用结构，但在2025年法庭裁决后，它目前无法收取佣金。Epic Games反对苹果的提议，认为它超出了法庭对应用商店垄断行为的指导。这场纠纷继续了两家公司之间关于佣金结构的持续法律诉讼。

title: US wait times for cancer surgeries are getting longer and longer
summary: Cancer surgery wait times in the US have reached a 10-year high, indicating delays in critical treatment access. The longer wait times may impact patient outcomes and reflect strain on healthcare resources. This trend raises concerns about treatment timeliness in the American healthcare system.
content: Study finds wait times for cancer surgeries hit 10-year high.

zh.title: 美国癌症手术等待时间越来越长
zh.summary: 美国的癌症手术等待时间达到了10年来的高点，表明关键治疗的获取出现延迟。较长的等待时间可能会影响患者预后，并反映医疗保健资源的压力。这一趋势引发了人们对美国医疗保健系统治疗及时性的担忧。

title: Investors sue Selena Gomez alleging fraud tied to her mental health startup
summary: Investors who contributed $1.2 million to Selena Gomez's mental health startup are filing a lawsuit alleging fraud over the company's development and marketing failures. The lawsuit questions Gomez's involvement in building and promoting the venture. The dispute highlights investor-founder conflicts in health tech startups.
content: The plaintiffs say they invested nearly $1.2 million in the company, and are accusing Gomez of failing to build and market the startup.

zh.title: 投资者控告塞琳娜·戈麦斯涉嫌欺诈其心理健康初创公司

title: Flock says its new tool will help identify police abuse, but hasn’t explained how it works
summary: Surveillance company Flock has made "Audit Assistance," a tool claiming to identify police abuse, mandatory for customers but without detailed public explanation of how it functions. The lack of transparency raises questions about the tool's actual effectiveness and mechanisms. This creates skepticism around Flock's commitment to preventing abuse despite the mandatory rollout.
content: The surveillance company announced it's making a tool called "Audit Assistance" mandatory for all customers, claiming it's already helped catch abuse. But the company has yet to explain how the tool works in detail, raising questions about its effectiveness.

title: ‘That is not acceptable’: Judge orders Google to make rival app store installs easier
summary: Judge James Donato ordered Google to simplify rival app store installations on Android devices, continuing enforcement from a three-year-old jury verdict finding Google maintained an illegal app monopoly. The ruling requires Google to feature rival stores within Google Play Store and provide competitors complete access. This order represents a significant step in breaking up Android's app distribution control.
content:
One month after Epic Games and Google seemingly stopped fighting over the future of Android app distribution, they were back in a San Francisco courtroom today - where Judge James Donato just ordered Google to make it easier to install rival app stores on Android. 
It's been nearly three years since a jury unanimously decided that Google had an illegal monopoly over Android apps, and almost two years since Judge Donato decided the best way of undoing that monopoly would be to crack open Android app distribution. Donato ordered Google to carry rival Android app stores inside its own Google Play Store, and to provide rivals with complecte acc …
Read the full story at The Verge.

zh.title: "这是不可接受的":法官命令谷歌使竞争应用商店的安装更容易
zh.summary: 法官詹姆斯·多纳托命令谷歌简化Android设备上竞争应用商店的安装,延续了三年前陪审团裁定谷歌维持非法应用垄断的执行。该裁定要求谷歌在Google Play商店中推荐竞争商店,并向竞争对手提供完全访问权限。此命令代表了打破Android应用分发控制的重大一步。

title: If Apple sends you a push notification alerting you to a spyware attack, take it seriously
summary: Apple has implemented push notifications to iPhone lock screens alerting users when the company detects government spyware targeting their devices. This proactive notification system aims to inform users of sophisticated surveillance threats targeting their accounts. The feature represents Apple's efforts to enhance device security transparency against state-sponsored threats.
content: Apple now sends out push notifications to iPhone lock screens when the company identifies government spyware targeting someone's devices.

title: The fight over Flock and other ALPRs
summary: Over 120,000 Flock automatic license plate reader cameras operate across the US, using AI to track vehicles and monitor movements nationwide. Multiple communities have canceled contracts or disabled the cameras due to privacy concerns about data collection, access, and usage. Amazon's Ring also ended its Flock partnership amid public backlash over surveillance implications.
content:
There are over 120,000 of Flock’s automatic license plate reader (ALPR) cameras installed all over the US. Flock’s cameras, and others like them, use AI to identify and track vehicles based on their license plate number, make, model, color, and other info, networked together to track vehicles and people’s movements throughout the day and across the country.
Dozens of communities have canceled contracts for the cameras or turned them off, including Los Angeles, as officials have pushed for more limits on the data they collect, who has access to it, and how it can be used in the future. Earlier this year, Amazon-owned Ring canceled a partnership with Flock after online backlash.

summary: Microsoft is retiring Mico, the animated yellow avatar that appeared in Copilot's voice mode, and moving it to the Learn Live platform. Mico, introduced last October as Copilot's interactive identity with real-time facial expressions, is being repositioned to a different context. The change reflects Microsoft's evolving approach to AI assistant design.
content:
Mico is headed to Learn Live. | Image: Microsoft	

Microsoft Copilot will no longer show its emotive yellow blob, Mico, when you use the chatbot's voice mode. In a support page, Microsoft says it's going to move Mico to its Learn Live platform, where the avatar will have "more to react to," as reported earlier by GeekWire.
Mico launched in Copilot's voice mode last October, with Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman pitching the avatar as a way to give the chatbot an "identity." The blob would react to what you say in real-time, complete with facial expressions and animations.

Mico joins the long list of virtual helpers that Microsoft has retired over the years, like Clippy, Cortana, and Rover …

A screenshot of Oxenfree II: Lost Signals from Night School Studio. | Image: Night School / Netflix	

Netflix plans to shut down two of its gaming studios, as reported by Game File and Variety, as it makes a bigger shift toward party games and titles streamed to TVs.
One of the studios being shut down is Night School Studio, creators of the Oxenfree series. Netflix bought Night School in 2021, and it just released a horror experience called Unhinged for TVs and launched a mobile game in 2025 tied to Black Mirror. The other studio that's set to close is Helsinki-based Moonloot Games, which was created in 2022.

title: I finally found a robot lawnmower I’d trust with my yard
summary: Modern robot lawnmowers have improved significantly, with advances in RTK navigation, all-wheel-drive, and obstacle avoidance making them reliable enough to maintain lawns with minimal oversight. After testing five models on a three-quarter-acre property, the reviewer found they produce consistently better results than traditional methods while operating quietly. The technology still requires some monitoring but substantially reduces yard maintenance work.
content:
From left, Segway, Roborock, Dreame, Husqvarna, and Mammotion automowers lined up to do battle with my lawn. | Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge	

Robot lawnmowers are finally good enough to take a lot of work out of maintaining a yard, but they’re still not set-it-and-forget-it machines. If you don’t want these autonomous cutting machines to tear up your lawn or go roaming in your neighbors’ yard, you’re still going to need to keep an eye on them. But with some oversight, they can take a big chore off your hands. 
This summer I tested five bots on my flat, three-quarter-acre, coastal South Carolina property with sandy soil, centipede grass, and lots of trees. Things went much better than last year’s trials and tribulations, thanks to huge improvements in navigation and maneuverability. Basically, they stopped getting stuck. My lawn has never looked better, and my spouse — who had sworn off robot lawnmowers after a user-error injury — is now a convert. His riding lawnmower has been idle for over a month.
The consistency of robot mowers is impressive. Running daily and shaving just millimeters at a time, these mowers have created a noticeably lusher lawn. I walked out on it barefoot this morning — something I’ve never done before. The best part is that they work quietly around the clock, without bothering my pets, the wildlife, or the neighbors. I also love the professional-looking lawn lines they make.
What’s better
The key upgrades this year are network RTK navigation, fallback navigation systems, and improved all-wheel-drive to tackle rougher terrain. 
RTK — real-time kinematic positioning — is the satellite positioning tech most automowers switched to over the last few years as they’ve ditched boundary wires. It uses stationary ground-based reference stations (antennas), along with GPS, to provide very precise location data, down to a centimeter or two. It’s used for surveying, drone navigation,  and anything that needs that fine level of precision.

The overhaul converts existing infrastructure for electric vehicle production as part of Ford's EV transition strategy. title: Meta adds AI screening to detect WhatsApp scams
summary: Meta has launched an optional Scam Alert feature on WhatsApp that uses on-device machine learning to identify and flag suspicious messages, rolling out in limited beta. When the AI detects a potential scam, users receive a warning visible only to them, allowing them to block, report, or continue. Users can also mark false positives to improve system accuracy.
content:
Meta is launching an optional Scam Alert feature on WhatsApp that uses on-device machine learning to flag suspicious messages. Earlier this year, Meta also launched scam detection for device linking requests on WhatsApp. The new Scam Alert feature, which is rolling out in a limited beta, shows users a warning if a chat seems like a scam:
If the model identifies a message as a likely scam attempt, the user sees a warning in the chat, which is not visible to the other person. title: Suno is trying to look more like a real music production tool

These improvements position Suno as a more serious music production tool for AI-generated audio creators.
content:
Suno is releasing Studio 2.0 with significant upgrades that push it closer to an actual digital audio workstation (DAW), rather than a bare-bones audio editor with generative AI features. Unfortunately, Suno Studio doesn't appear to support third-party plugins or VSTs yet, so you're stuck using its proprietary built-in synth. That synth appears to be a basic two-oscillator wavetable plugin with three envelopes and four LFOs.

title: Nintendo’s next Fire Emblem has a bold new structure
summary: Nintendo's new Fire Emblem game for Switch 2, Fortune's Weave, allows players to swap between four heroes and pursue multiple storylines simultaneously, addressing a longstanding limitation of Three Houses where players typically experienced only one faction's story per playthrough. This structural shift aims to let players see all character narratives in a single run.
